To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thioester of 2,4-dodecapentenoic acid, a proposed intermediate in the biosynthetic pathway to the antifungal antibiotic HSAF, was synthesized, and the thioester was tested in a purified nonribosmal peptide synthetase, but no incorporation of the thioester into HSAF or any other product was observed.

we have developed a new method to synthesize an analog of a proposed intermediate in the biosynthetic pathway of Heat Stable Antigun Factor (HSA) and that we have investigated this analog as a substrate for the nonribosomal peptide biosynthesis of this natural product.

we have developed a method to synthesize a 2, 4, 6, 8, 10-dodecapentaenoate thioester as an analog of a proposed intermediate for biosynthesis of HSAF, a natural product that is a potent antifungal agent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of synthetic methods for the synthesis of a 2-alkenoic acid thioesters as substrates for biosynthetic studies of HSAF.
the synthesis of a 2-4-6-8-10-dodecapentaenoate thioester as substrate for biosynthesis.
the development of synthetic methodology for the preparation of thioester substrates for the biosynthesis of HSAF and related compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the thioester was not incorporated in HSAF.
the SNAC ester of dodecapentanoate was not a substrate for biosynthetic incorporation into HSAF.
the SNAC ester of dodecapentanoate is not incorporated into the HSAF biosynthesis pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HSAF biosynthesis is not initiated with the N-acetylcysamine thioester of a 2-enoate.
the thioester was not a substrate for the biosynthesis of HSAF.
we have developed a synthetic route to a thioester of a 12-membered fatty acid, and that the thioester was not incorporated into the products of the HSAF NRPS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biosynthetic machinery for HSAF is highly selective and that the thioester is a poor substrate for the biosynthetic enzyme.
the thioester of the 2,4-dodecadienoic acid is a stable substrate for the nonribosomal peptide system.
the synthesis and characterization of a thioester substrate for the HSAF biosynthetic machinery is feasible and that the substrate is not incorporated in the biosynthesis.
